text: Digital archive corruption, Library of Congress 1987: Database contains 40,000 card catalog entries for books that don't exist. When librarians attempt deletion, entries multiply. Books occasionally appear on shelves overnight.

Botanical survey, Amazon Basin 1889: Expedition catalogued tree species that photosynthesize moonlight. Specimens collected during new moon phases continued growing in complete darkness for eighteen months.

Archaeological anomaly 2019: Roman villa excavation, Pompeii, uncovered mosaic depicting WiFi symbol with Latin inscription SIGNAL WEAK HERE TOO. Tesserae composition authentic to 79 CE. Network name: VESUVIUSGUEST.

Personnel file, Sears Department Store 1963: Employee Harold Kemper worked register 7 for thirtyone years. Store only had six registers. Payroll continued until 1994. No record of Harold Kemper's hire date or existence.

Meteorological report, Damascus 1401: Clouds formed geometric patterns spelling out next week's grain prices in Arabic script. Predictions proved accurate to the dinar. Sky remained illiterate until 1823.

Census data, Prague 1572: Population recorded as 47,000 living residents plus 3,200 formerly living but administratively active. Tax records show the formerly living paid promptly. Death certificates for this group dated 1598.

Surgical report, Vienna General Hospital 1894: Patient's appendix contained fully formed pocket watch, ticking accurately. Timepiece showed correct hour despite patient never owning a watch. Inscription: Property of Future Self.

Biological survey, Orkney Islands 1756: Sheep flock observed grazing in perfect spiral formation, completing one revolution every 47 minutes. Wool samples contained geometric patterns not present during shearing. Flock disbanded at sunset,

Library catalog, Alexandria 47 BCE: Book titled Complete History of Rome Through 476 CE shelved correctly despite Rome's fall occurring five centuries later. Text accuracy verified by modern historians. Author listed as Anonymous Future.

Property deed, Salem 1692: House sold to buyer who existed only on Wednesdays. Neighbors confirmed regular occupancy despite buyer's intermittent ontological status. Property taxes paid in full, receipt signed Conditionally Yours.

Personal diary, recovered from Pompeii excavation: Final entry dated August 25th, 79 CE describes tomorrow's ash rain in past tense. Handwriting analysis confirms single author throughout. Volcano erupted August 24th.

Census data, Reykjavik 1801: Population recorded as 5,406 residents plus one recurring stranger. Enumeration notes describe individual who appears in different households each count, aging normally between surveys but never dying.

Archaeological survey, Babylon 1750 BCE: Construction workers unearthed foundation stone inscribed Renovated 1750 BCE Original built 1750 BCE. Stone shows no signs of prior construction. Building exists in continuous present tense.

Medical records, St. Bartholomew's Hospital 1348: Patient admitted with plague symptoms recovers after consuming bread that won't be invented until 1928. Baker's apprentice claims recipe came to him in dreams of white coats and sterile room

Weather station logs, Nome Alaska 1952: Temperature recorded as 40F while thermometer simultaneously displayed 98F. Both readings accurate. Station operator reported feeling both frostbite and heat stroke within same hour.
